# powerdns / fuzz_target_dnslabeltext_parseRFC1035CharString

powerdns's own fuzz target `fuzz_target_dnslabeltext_parseRFC1035CharString` ([source](source/fuzz_dnslabeltext_parseRFC1035CharString.cc), unmodified), one of the targets OSS-Fuzz builds, over pdns 2.2.0-alpha0 (PowerDNS/pdns at 114b76ca).

parseRFC1035CharString(input, val) (the ragel-generated TXT character-string unescaper); output and return value discarded; not even exceptions are caught.

## How this program differs from what OSS-Fuzz runs
- Linked against pdns 2.2.0-alpha0 at commit 114b76ca with 2 patches to the library (listed on the project page).
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the harness one to four times and prints each return value.

## What the harness checks
The harness makes no check of its own beyond not crashing, so a statement about it says only that the code it calls never crashes, hangs or trips a sanitizer.
